old: Amines are prepared mainly by five routes. Nitro compounds are reduced with $Sn/HCl$, $Fe/HCl$ or $H_2/Pd$; $Fe/HCl$ is preferred because the $FeCl_2$ formed is hydrolysed back to $HCl$. Alkyl halides undergo ammonolysis, but this gives a mixture of 1°, 2° and 3° amines and the quaternary salt. Nitriles and amides are reduced with $LiAlH_4$ or $Na/C_2H_5OH$. Gabriel phthalimide synthesis gives pure 1° aliphatic amines only. Hofmann bromamide degradation gives a 1° amine with one carbon fewer than the amide. Lower amines are gases or liquids with a fishy smell. Their boiling points are lower than those of alcohols because N-H...N hydrogen bonds are weaker than O-H...O bonds. Key reactions are alkylation, acylation, benzoylation, the carbylamine reaction, reaction with $HNO_2$ and electrophilic substitution in aniline. Amines are used in dyes, drugs and polymers.
